name: es30-transform-feedback
title: Transform feedback: capture, objects, pause/resume, queries
summary: Vertex shader outputs recorded into buffers: INTERLEAVED and SEPARATE modes, glBindBufferBase/Range, transform feedback objects (per-object binding state, two-buffer ping-pong), pause/resume, TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_PRIMITIVES_WRITTEN queries, glGetTransformFeedbackVarying, RASTERIZER_DISCARD, a GPU particle step drawn in a second pass, and the errors the specification defines while a capture is active. Buffers are compared bit for bit and every pixel with a CPU model.
spec: ES 3.0 §2.10.1.1 Binding Buffer Objects to Indexed Targets (BindBufferBase/BindBufferRange)
ES 3.0 §2.12.8 Output Variables (TransformFeedbackVaryings, GetTransformFeedbackVarying, link failures)
ES 3.0 §2.15 Transform Feedback, §2.15.1 Transform Feedback Objects, §2.15.2 Transform Feedback Primitive Capture
ES 3.0 §6.1.7 Asynchronous Queries, §6.1.9 Buffer Object Queries (indexed TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_BUFFER_* queries), §6.1.11 Transform Feedback Queries
ES 3.0 §2.5 GL Errors, Table 6.24 Transform Feedback State, Table 6.34 Implementation Dependent Transform Feedback Limits
ES 3.1 §12.1 and ES 3.2 §12.2.1-12.2.2, Table 12.1, §12.3 (the draw-mode and buffer-overflow rules changed in ES 3.2)
GLSL ES 3.00 §4.3.6 Output Variables (flat integer outputs), §7.1 Vertex Shader Special Variables

api.glTransformFeedbackVaryings: INTERLEAVED (step, warp, probe) and SEPARATE (stream) lists declared before linking; the captured values equal the CPU model; SEPARATE with count > MAX_TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_SEPARATE_ATTRIBS -> INVALID_VALUE; unknown or duplicate names fail to link; the list order is the capture order
api.glGetTransformFeedbackVarying: name, type and size of a float, an int, an array (FLOAT_VEC2 size 2) and gl_Position, in list order; bufSize truncation; index >= count -> INVALID_VALUE with unmodified outputs
api.glBeginTransformFeedback: POINTS / LINES / TRIANGLES captures compared with the CPU model; TRIANGLE_STRIP -> INVALID_ENUM; while active, paused, with no buffer, no program or no varyings -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glEndTransformFeedback: ends the capture (ACTIVE/PAUSED queries), implicit resume while paused; while inactive -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glPauseTransformFeedback: draws while paused are not recorded or counted; ACTIVE stays TRUE, PAUSED TRUE; while inactive or paused -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glResumeTransformFeedback: appends right after the last record before the pause; with another program current or when not paused -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glGenTransformFeedbacks: two ping-pong objects plus a scratch object; a generated name is not an object until first bound
api.glBindTransformFeedback: TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_BINDING and per-object binding state; allowed while paused, INVALID_OPERATION while active, for a deleted name and for a never generated name
api.glIsTransformFeedback: FALSE for 0, for a generated but never bound name and after deletion; TRUE after the first bind
api.glDeleteTransformFeedbacks: deleting an inactive object is silent, 0 and unused names are ignored, the active object -> INVALID_OPERATION and survives
api.glBindBufferBase: binding points 0-2, per-object indexed binding queries, START/SIZE reset to 0; while capturing (also while paused) -> INVALID_OPERATION; index >= MAX -> INVALID_VALUE
api.glBindBufferRange: three SEPARATE streams in ranges at offsets 0/100/260 of one buffer (gaps untouched); a range smaller than the buffer limits the capture; offset or size not a multiple of 4, size 0, negative offset, index >= MAX -> INVALID_VALUE; while capturing -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glGetIntegeri_v: TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_BUFFER_BINDING per index and per object; index = MAX_TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_SEPARATE_ATTRIBS -> INVALID_VALUE
api.glGetInteger64i_v: TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_BUFFER_START and _SIZE after BindBufferBase (0) and BindBufferRange (offset, size)
api.glGetBooleanv: TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_ACTIVE / _PAUSED through begin, pause, resume, end and object switches; RASTERIZER_DISCARD
api.glGenQueries: one TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_PRIMITIVES_WRITTEN query object reused for every count
api.glIsQuery: FALSE before the first glBeginQuery, TRUE after
api.glBeginQuery: resets the count; counts 8 (3+5 points), 2, 4 (query opened after glBeginTransformFeedback), 352 (11 steps into two objects), 6 (paused draws not counted), 0 while transform feedback is inactive
api.glEndQuery: closes the count; CURRENT_QUERY returns to 0
api.glGetQueryiv: CURRENT_QUERY is 0 when idle and the query's name while active
api.glGetQueryObjectuiv: QUERY_RESULT drives the draw counts of the second passes; QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE becomes TRUE; the active query -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glEnable: RASTERIZER_DISCARD: with it on, the capture pass draws no pixel and still records the same data
api.glDisable: RASTERIZER_DISCARD off: the same capture also draws its red points (pixels compared); glClear then works again
api.glClear: ignored while RASTERIZER_DISCARD is enabled (cell stays at the old clear color), works when it is disabled
api.glDrawArrays: the capture and the second-pass draws; every primitive type allowed for each capture mode; mismatching types -> INVALID_OPERATION; ES 3.2 overflow behavior
api.glDrawArraysInstanced: instance 0's vertices are recorded before instance 1's (gl_InstanceID in the capture); mismatching type -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glDrawElements: while capturing: INVALID_OPERATION in ES 3.0/3.1, allowed and recorded for POINTS in ES 3.2; drawn while paused without being recorded
api.glDrawElementsInstanced: while capturing: same rule as glDrawElements
api.glDrawRangeElements: while capturing: same rule as glDrawElements
api.glUseProgram: while capturing and not paused -> INVALID_OPERATION; allowed while paused (resume then needs the original program)
api.glLinkProgram: of the program used by an active capture -> INVALID_OPERATION and the program stays linked; link failures for bad varying names
api.glMapBufferRange: reads every captured buffer back (through the TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_BUFFER target) for the bit-exact comparison with the CPU model
api.glBufferData: sentinel-filled capture buffers: bytes that were not written stay 0xA5
api.glVertexAttribPointer: the captured buffers are the vertex data of the second pass (strides 32, 20, 8/12/4 at offsets 0/100/260); observed through pixels
api.glEnableVertexAttribArray: attribute arrays of the capture and render passes; observed through captured data and pixels
api.glGenVertexArrays: nine VAOs for the capture inputs and second-pass sources
api.glBindVertexArray: VAO switching selects each pass's inputs
api.glUniform1f: u_dt (1/16 or 0) and u_floor change the captured simulation exactly as the CPU model predicts
api.glUniform4f: u_color: the red points that appear when RASTERIZER_DISCARD is off

visual_review.notes: Viewed the gpu, llvmpipe and zink es-max captures (256x256, identical to the eye; the checks report 0/255 deviation on every driver). Top left: a 4x4 grid of sixteen differently colored quads (greens/yellows in the top row, blues/purples/magentas in the bottom row), each sheared and the whole grid bowed by the warp, with dark gaps between the quads. Top right: four rows of eight small squares in the lower half of the cell forming nested arcs (the bounced row at the bottom, higher rows above), colors graded by column and row. Bottom left: one horizontal row with three green squares, a visible gap of two missing slots, then three pink/magenta squares. Bottom right: a 4x3 lattice of twelve squares in three sizes (6, 8, 10 px) with distinct colors. Dark-blue clear color elsewhere; no red pixels anywhere (nothing leaked past RASTERIZER_DISCARD) and no stray marks. Window-size review (claude-opus-5.5): gpu capture at 333x777 (and 1000x200) viewed: the same four cells stretched to the 2x2 halves of the surface (the warped quad grid tall and narrow in the top left, the point rows in the top right, the 3 + 3 pause row and the 4x3 stream lattice at the bottom); point squares keep their pixel size, no red pixels.
